ns1:item.dc:creator: Alberto Bortolotti Tuna Taşan-Kok a Department of Architecture and Urban Studies, Politecnico di Milano, Milano, Italyb Department of Human Geography, Planning, and International Development Studies, University of Amsterdam, Amsterdam, NetherlandsDr. Alberto Bortolotti is Adjunct Professor and Postdoctoral Researcher in Urban Planning at the Department of Architecture and Urban Studies (DAStU) of Politecnico di Milano, where he obtained his PhD. He is the author of books, essays and articles on the interactions between finance and space. Between 2021 and 2025, he served as Vice-President of the Order of Architects, Planners, Landscape Architects and Conservationists of Milan. He has been a Visiting Researcher at the University of Amsterdam and KU Leuven, where he explored real estate actors, processes, and markets in depth. He has also worked as a policy advisor on housing and urban policies for the Lombardy Region, the Italian Ministry of Culture, the European Parliament, and, as a researcher, for the Ebert Foundation, the Foundation for European Progressive Studies, and the Feltrinelli Foundation.Prof. Dr. Tuna Taşan-Kok is Chair of Urban Governance and Planning at the University of Amsterdam, where she leads the Urban Planning Research Program Group. Her research focuses on urban governance, with particular attention to property-led urban development and the intersections between planning regulation and property investment flows. She explores how these dynamics shape cities, influence institutional change, and open up or constrain pathways toward socially just and sustainable urban futures. Her work combines political economy perspectives with relational approaches to governance, and engages with innovative policy and planning practices. Prof. Taşan-Kok is the co-founder and Chair of UGoveRN (Urban Governance Research Network – www.ugovern.eu), an international platform connecting scholars and practitioners in the field of urban governance. She is widely published and internationally recognized for her contributions to urban planning, human geography, and governance studies, and is actively involved in editorial, advisory, and interdisciplinary research initiatives.

ns1:item.dc:creator: Omar Ben Haman Urban and Regional Planning College of Business, Creative Arts, Law and Social Sciences, Flinders University, Adelaide, AustraliaDr Omar Ben Haman is a Lecturer in Urban and Regional Planning at Flinders University and an urban sociologist whose research explores the intersections of planning, housing, informality, urban design, and social inequality. His work examines how planning and housing systems shape the lives of vulnerable and marginalised communities, with a focus on creating more inclusive and socially responsive urban futures. He is a full member of the Planning Institute of Australia, serves on the editorial board of the Journal of Social Service Research, and has published widely in national and international journals.
